title: How to become a business loan broker (without pretending it’s easy)
excerpt: A realistic path: niche, list, script, docs, packaging, follow-up. What to do first, and what to stop doing immediately.
seoTitle: How to become a business loan broker — realistic steps & process
seoDescription: A blunt guide to becoming a business loan broker: the weekly plan, qualification script, docs, and how commissions really happen.

sections.title: Choose your lane: referral vs broker vs agency
paragraphs: If you only want to refer leads, your payout is usually smaller and your control is limited. If you want broker-level commissions, you need broker-level work: qualification, packaging, and follow-up.
The fastest way to fail is to mix lanes. Decide what you are selling and what you are responsible for.
bullets: Referral: simple, smaller payouts, low control
Agency: highest upside, you own operations

sections.title: Pipeline is the job
paragraphs: Most affiliates lose because they have no pipeline. They have screenshots and excitement. A pipeline is numbers: attempts, conversations, qualified, docs collected, submitted, funded.
If you can’t build a list of 100 businesses, you don’t have a business.

sections.title: Qualification: ask the questions everyone avoids
paragraphs: Time in business and revenue range are not rude questions. They are the difference between a file that closes and a week of wasted follow-ups.
Ask for docs early. You are not selling a dream; you are packaging a file.

title: Business loan broker commission: what’s real vs what’s marketing
excerpt: Commission rate means nothing without approval reality. Here’s how splits, CPA, tiers, and clawbacks actually work.

sections.title: Commission models you’ll see
paragraphs: CPA is simple but typically smaller. Splits are larger but require more work. Tiered programs reward volume or quality. Rev share is rare and often comes with fine print.
Always ask what triggers payout, what voids payout, and whether there are clawbacks.

sections.title: The approval rate reality check
paragraphs: If a program claims huge payouts with zero qualification, the math doesn’t math. Approval reality matters more than the headline commission.
Your job is to deliver fundable files, not to collect “interested” leads.

title: Make money referring business loans (without becoming a spammer)
excerpt: Referral income is real—if you qualify and protect trust. Here’s how to do it with a niche and a clean process.

sections.title: Trust is the asset
paragraphs: If you burn your network with bait-and-switch terms, you’re done. Referral income compounds only when trust stays intact.
Under-promise, over-deliver, and be honest about timelines and approvals.

sections.title: Niche beats generic outreach
paragraphs: A niche gives you scripts, objections, and proof. Generic “need funding?” messages get ignored.
Pick a niche you can speak about without googling during the call.

title: CPA business loan referrals: how to structure the relationship
excerpt: If you work with CPAs, you need clean expectations, compliance awareness, and a process that protects the client relationship.

sections.title: Align incentives and expectations
paragraphs: CPAs care about client outcomes and reputation. Your process must be clean and transparent.
Agree on what gets referred, what disqualifies a file, and how updates will be shared.

title: Best business loan affiliate programs: what “best” actually means
excerpt: “Best” depends on your lane. Here’s how to pick based on cycle time, docs, product fit, and your ability to sell.

sections.title: Criteria that matter more than marketing
paragraphs: Payout is not the only variable. Look at cycle time, product fit, support quality, and whether the program punishes poor qualification.
If the program tolerates spam, it will attract spam. That hurts everyone.

title: Business loan affiliate playbook: Week 1 (ship the basics)
excerpt: If you do nothing else, do these five things this week. This is how you stop researching and start earning.

sections.title: The five actions
paragraphs: Pick a niche. Build a list of 100. Run 10 real conversations. Ask for docs early. Submit clean files.
Everything else is procrastination dressed as strategy.
